md:
### Early right heart failure after LVAD at a glance

| Item | What the notes say |
|---|---|
| Presentation | Failure to wean from bypass, or low or falling output and blood pressure with high or rising CVP and escalating inotropes and vasopressors, without another cause such as tamponade |
| Trial definition | Need for RV support (RVAD or VA ECMO) or prolonged inotropes (over 1 to 2 weeks) |
| Haemodynamic criteria used (no agreed definition) | CI under 2.0 L/min/m², MAP 55 mmHg or less, CVP over 15 mmHg, SvO2 55% or less, more than 10 mcg/kg/min dobutamine or equivalent |
| PAPi | (PA systolic − PA diastolic) / RA pressure; no single threshold; means of 1.3 to 1.8 reported in severe post-LVAD RHF |
| Causes | Intrinsic RV dysfunction, high PVR, bypass injury, loss of pericardial restraint, LV over-decompression, sternal compression of the RV, reduced LV contractility and twist |
| Exclude first | Tamponade (bleeding) or sternal compression (I, C); delayed sternal closure is reasonable with excessive bleeding, thoracic oedema or RV distension |
| Medical | Early inotrope (dobutamine, low-dose dopamine) or milrinone; vasopressor with inotropic action if hypotensive; avoid both hypovolaemia and RV distension (CVP/PAOP ratio under 1); lower PVR with LV unloading, fluid removal and inhaled NO or prostacyclins; avoid over-decompressing the LV |
| Mechanical | Early surgical or percutaneous RVAD for refractory RV failure (I, C); planned RVAD for high-risk patients before shock worsens (IIb, C); unplanned RVAD carried 50% in-hospital mortality (Takeda) |

Source: summarised from "Early right heart failure" in this section (ISHLT 2023 MCS guideline, Task Force 3).
anchor: Planned RVAD in patients with high-risk pre-operative features, before cardiogenic shock worsens

md:
### Early ICU care: isolated LVAD against BiVAD and total artificial heart

| | Isolated LVAD | BiVAD or TAH |
|---|---|---|
| Heparin starts | Within 24 h once haemostasis is secure and drain output under 50 mL for several hours (at least 8 h after surgery) | Not in the first 24 h; then UFH once haemostasis is secured |
| Heparin target | aPTT 40 to 60 s, moving to the upper end after a few days | aPTT 50 to 70 s; 60 to 75 s after 48 h (SynCardia and BiVAD table) |
| Warfarin | From day 2 to 3 once enteral absorption is adequate; INR 2 to 3 | After all chest drains are out; INR typically 2.5 to 3.0, 2.5 to 3.5 for SynCardia; DOACs not indicated (III, C) |
| Aspirin | 81 to 325 mg from day 1 to 3 | Once bleeding has stopped, low dose; use sparingly in BiVADs |
| MAP goal | 75 to 90 mmHg | 65 to 80 mmHg (BiVAD) |
| Output | Drugs to keep CI over 2.2 L/min/m² (I, C) | Device flow for CI over 2.2 (I, A); left flow 5 to 10% above right |
| PA catheter | Swan-Ganz for output, SvO2, PA pressure and PVR (I, C) | BiVAD: thermodilution unreliable, may be reasonable for SvO2 (IIb, C); TAH: cannot be placed, use an LA line (LAP 8 to 16, CVP 12 to 15 mmHg) |
| Arrest | Defibrillation safe (I, B); compressions if unconscious without adequate perfusion (IIa, B) | TAH: no CPR, defibrillation or pacing (III, C) |

Source: summarised from this section and the earlier LVAD sections of this tab ("Early ICU management after durable LVAD" and "arrhythmias and cardiac arrest in LVAD inpatients"), ISHLT 2023 MCS guideline Task Forces 3, 4 and 8.

md:
### Right heart failure risk before LVAD at a glance

| Item | What the 2023 guideline says |
|---|---|
| Why it happens | RV–PA uncoupling after transient (volume, ischaemia) and structural (septal shift, apical coring) changes, plus more venous return once the pump starts: RV dilatation, TR, leftward septal shift |
| Clinical risk factors for biventricular support | Chemotherapy cardiomyopathy, cardiogenic shock, VA-ECMO before LVAD, pre-implant phosphodiesterase inhibitor use |
| Haemodynamic predictors | RA/PCWP ratio (the classic one); RV stroke work (needs Fick output); PAPi under 1.85 ± 0.1; RA pressure with PA elastance; a Y descent as deep as or deeper than the X descent; no single afterload index identifies RHF alone |
| Right heart catheter | Urgent: to guide diuresis, inotropes or temporary MCS, with a PA catheter in ICU before surgery; elective: within 1 to 2 weeks of surgery |
| Optimise | CVP 15 mmHg or less before LVAD; IV loop diuretic with thiazide adjunct; ultrafiltration only after diuretics, inotropes and temporary MCS have been tried |
| Cautions | Pulmonary vasodilators can raise left-sided filling pressures; pre-operative sildenafil was linked to more RV failure |
| If the RV stays poor | ECMO or planned BiVAD; planned BiVAD may do better than unplanned or delayed |

Source: summarised from "Right heart assessment before LVAD" and "RV optimisation before LVAD" in this section (ISHLT 2023 MCS guideline, Task Force 2).
anchor: Poor RV or refractory biventricular failure: ECMO or planned BiVAD

md:
### Who recovers on an LVAD: predictors at a glance

| Source | Predictors of recovery |
|---|---|
| Clinical | Non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy (recovers about 4 times as often as ischaemic), younger (under 40 to 50), shorter heart failure history (under 1 to 5 years) |
| Echo on full support (should trigger low-speed testing) | Normal LVEDD, better wall motion, MR and AR absent or grade 1 or less, no RV dilatation, TR grade 2 or less, more frequent aortic valve opening at unchanged speed |
| Dandel (off pump) | LVEF 50% or more with LVEDD 55 mm or less or heart failure for 5 years or less; or LVEF 45% or more with LVEDD 55 mm or less and heart failure for 5 years or less: best predictors of over 5-year stability after explant |
| I-CARS (INTERMACS) | Age under 50, non-ischaemic, under 2 years from diagnosis, no ICD, creatinine 1.2 mg/dl or less, LVEDD under 6.5 cm |
| Other | Pre-LVAD speckle-tracking rotational mechanics (sensitivity 92%, specificity 73%); lower pre-LVAD inflammatory markers; short ryanodine receptor to sarcolemma distance |

Source: summarised from "Who recovers" in this section (ISHLT 2023 MCS guideline, Task Force 7).
